title: A Vow for the Bakery
premise: Edmund Galloway, a pastry chef drowning in debt and grief over his late mother's recipes, agrees to a fake date with Marisol Vega, a sharp-tongued food journalist, to survive his family reunion. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens as Marisol discovers the story behind his failing café — and the predatory lender circling it. When Marisol is offered the career-making exposé that could expose the lender but also destroy Edmund's last chance at refinancing, she must choose between ambition and love. In the end, Edmund's found family of regulars rallies to buy back the bakery's debt, Marisol publishes the truth on her own terms, and they open the doors together — not as a fake date, but as partners.
about_author: Jonah Iversen is a former line cook who traded kitchen shifts for quiet mornings writing love stories set in small businesses on the brink. He lives in a coastal town where he still judges every café by its morning bun.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet Edmund counting coins behind the counter of Galloway's, his late mother's café, as a final notice arrives from lender Corvin Capital. His sister texts about the family reunion requiring a plus-one. Emotional beat: weary pride masking panic; Edmund decides he'd rather fake a relationship than admit failure.

chapters.title: The Interview
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Food journalist Marisol Vega visits Galloway's for a 'rising bakeries' piece, but her editor wants her hunting a bigger story about Corvin Capital's predatory loans. She notices Edmund's flinch at the lender's name. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into recognition — two people performing competence while quietly unraveling.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund awkwardly proposes the fake-date arrangement; Marisol, needing access to reunion guest Uncle Ray — a retired judge with Corvin ties — accepts. They draft rules over burnt scones. Emotional beat: playful banter layered over mutual loneliness; both pretend this is purely business.

chapters.title: The Reunion
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the Galloway family estate, Marisol plays the girlfriend flawlessly, charming Edmund's skeptical grandmother and deflecting his smug cousin. But when Edmund defends her against a cruel joke, the performance cracks into something real. Emotional beat: warmth arriving uninvited; first genuine touch, held one beat too long.

chapters.title: What the Recipe Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Marisol stays late helping him recreate his mother's lost cinnamon knot recipe from memory and taste. He tells her about his mother's death and why the café can't fail. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes intimacy; Edmund realizes he's stopped acting, and it terrifies him.

chapters.title: Uncle Ray's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol gets Uncle Ray talking; he confirms Corvin Capital engineers defaults to seize properties, including Galloway's building. Her editor offers a front-page feature — with Edmund as the anonymous cautionary tale. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into dread; the story that could save others will bury him.

chapters.title: Dessert and Deception
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund discovers Marisol's notes naming him as a source. The fight is brutal — he feels used, she insists exposure was their only weapon. She walks out; he signs nothing, alone with the final notice. Emotional beat: heartbreak at the exact moment trust mattered most; the fake date dies so something honest might begin.

chapters.title: The Regulars
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Devastated, Edmund nearly surrenders the keys — until his regulars, the found family he never counted, arrive: the retired teacher, the night-shift nurse, the kid who does homework in booth three. They've pooled savings to buy the debt from Corvin before foreclosure. Emotional beat: grace he didn't earn; Edmund learns second chances are made, not timed.

chapters.title: Print It Anyway
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol publishes the exposé with Edmund's full consent, obtained in a rain-soaked reconciliation outside the café — names, faces, and all. Corvin Capital collapses under scrutiny; Ray testifies. Emotional beat: courage chosen over safety; Marisol sacrifices the anonymous scoop for the true one, choosing him without abandoning herself.

chapters.title: A Vow for the Bakery
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Months later, Galloway's reopens co-owned by Edmund and his regulars, Marisol's byline framed beside his mother's recipe card. On the anniversary of the fake date, Edmund proposes — not with a ring first, but with the cinnamon knot they finally got right. Emotional beat: full-circle joy; memory honored, justice won, love no longer pretending.
